Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Travel & transport

bus noun

also coach, school bus, tour bus, bus timetable, does the bus stop in …?, bus driver, coach (tour bus)

modern

M-O s.v. bus, citing Albert, Helfer and Bacci
Traupman 215

autoraeda longa

bus or coach

The noun is autoraeda, autoraedae f..

Other words

  • autocīnētum lāophoricum

    also used · modern

    A learned alternative. The Greek-derived lāo- reflects “people,” and -cīnēt- “moving.”

  • lāophorum, lāophorī n.

    noun, second declension · also used · modern

  • autoraeda pūblica — public bus

    also used · modern

    Also recorded in the modern lexicon.

  • raeda longa

    also used · modern · Traupman 284: bus, raeda longa; Andresian p. 40

    The same phrase as autoraeda longa, without auto-.

  • coenautocīnētum, coenautocīnētī n. — a bus (literally “a shared motor vehicle”)

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 215, 218, 396

Examples

  • Autoraedā longā īmus.

    We’re going by bus.composed

  • coenautocīnētum periēgēticum

    a tour busTraupman 218

  • hōrārium autoraedārum longārum

    a bus timetableTraupman 218

  • Subsistitne autoraeda longa in …?

    Does the bus stop in …?Traupman 218

  • coenautocīnētī gubernātor

    a bus driverTraupman 284

  • Subsistitne autoraeda longa (trāmen) in …?

    Does the bus (train) stop in …?Traupman 385

  • coenautocīnētum perigēticum

    a tour busTraupman 396

See also car.

SourcesMorgan–Owens: bus

Lewis & Short: raeda
